card.statement:
(a) Each square
matrix $A$ over an
algebraically closed
field $\mathbb F$ of
characteristic
different from $2$ is
congruent to a direct
sum, determined
uniquely up to
permutation of
summands, of
tridiagonal matrices
of three types:

\begin{equation}
\begin{bmatrix}
0&1 &&&0\\
\lambda&0&1 \\
&\lambda &0&\ddots&\\
&&\ddots&\ddots&1 \\
0&&&\lambda &0
\end{bmatrix}_{2k},\qquad
\lambda
\in\mathbb F,\
\lambda\ne \pm 1,
\end{equation}

in which each nonzero
$\lambda$ is
determined up to
replacement by
$\lambda^{-1}$
$($i.e., the matrices
<<ref:cm1>> with
$\lambda$ and
$\lambda^{-1}$ are
congruent$)$;

\begin{equation}
\begin{bmatrix}
\varepsilon &1&&&&0\\
-1&0&1&\\
&1&0&1&\\
&&-1&0&1&\\
&&&1&0&\ddots&\\
0&&&&  \ddots&\ddots
\end{bmatrix}_{n},
\quad
\begin{aligned}
&\text{$\varepsilon
=1$ if $n$ is a
multiple
of $4$,}\\
&\text{$\varepsilon
\in\{0,1\}$
otherwise};
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

and

\begin{equation}
\begin{bmatrix}
0 &1&&&&0\\
1&0&1&\\
&-1&0&1&\\
&&1&0&1\\
&&&-1&0&\ddots&\\
0&&&&  \ddots&\ddots\\
\end{bmatrix}_{4k}.
\qquad\qquad
\qquad\qquad
\qquad
\end{equation}

The subscripts $2k,\
n$, and $4k$ $($with
$k,n\in\mathbb N)$
designate the sizes of
the corresponding
matrices.

(b) The direct
sum asserted in
(a) is determined
uniquely up to
permutation of
summands by the
Kronecker canonical
form of $(A^T,A)$ for
equivalence. For each
direct summand $B$ of
types
<<ref:cm1>>--<<ref:cm3>>,
the Kronecker
canonical form of
$(B^T,B)$ is given in
the following table:

\begin{equation}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
\hline $B$& Kronecker
canonical form of $
(B^T,B)$\\
\hline\hline Matrix
<<ref:cm1>>&
$(I_k,J_k(\lambda))\oplus
(J_k(\lambda),I_k)$\\\hline
Matrix <<ref:cm2>>&
$(F_k,G_k)\oplus
(F_k^T,G_k^T)\ $ if
$n=2k+1$\\
with $\varepsilon=0$&
$(I_k,J_k(-1))\oplus
(I_k,J_k(-1))\ $ if
$n=2k$ $(k$ is
odd$)$\\\hline
$\begin{matrix}
\text{Matrix
<<ref:cm2>>}\\
\text{with
$\varepsilon=1$}
\end{matrix}$
&
$(I_n,J_n((-1)^{n+1})$
\\\hline
Matrix <<ref:cm3>>&
$(I_{2k},J_{2k}(1))\oplus
(I_{2k},J_{2k}(1))$\\\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{equation}
card.label: Theorem 1

paper.title: Tridiagonal canonical matrices of bilinear or sesquilinear forms and of pairs of symmetric, skew-symmetric, or Hermitian forms
paper.abstract: Tridiagonal canonical forms of square matrices under congruence or *congruence, pairs of symmetric or skew-symmetric matrices under congruence, and pairs of Hermitian matrices under *congruence are given over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2.
